proposal.title: Trump Issues Covington Memorandum on Clearances and Contracts
proposal.description_short: A February 25, 2025 presidential memorandum directed reviews of specified Covington clearances and federal contracts.
proposal.description_medium: On February 25, 2025, President Donald Trump issued a memorandum directing agencies to suspend specified security clearances held by Covington personnel who assisted former special counsel Jack Smith, end firm engagements where lawful, and have OMB review government contracts with the firm. proposal.description_long: On February 25, 2025, President Donald Trump issued a presidential memorandum addressed to the Secretaries of State, Defense and Energy, the attorney general, and the directors of several intelligence, personnel and budget agencies. The memorandum directed agencies to suspend, pending review, active security clearances held by Peter Koski and Covington & Burling members, partners or employees who had assisted former special counsel Jack Smith. It also instructed agencies to end the firm’s government engagements to the maximum extent permitted by law, asked OPM to circulate the memorandum to other clearance-granting agencies, and directed OMB to issue guidance for reviewing federal contracts with Covington. Each directive was qualified by applicable law. The White House text establishes what the memorandum ordered; it does not establish that every clearance was suspended, every contract was terminated, or that a review found misconduct. The document was a presidential memorandum, not the March 14 executive order described in the original entry. The proposed record reports the issuance and terms of the memorandum, not its later implementation.

proposal.title: Deutsche Bank Group Finances Chicago Trump Tower in 2005
proposal.description_short: In 2005, a lender group including Deutsche Bank made a $640 million construction loan for Trump International Hotel and Tower in Chicago, The Washington Post reported.
proposal.description_medium: The Washington Post reported that a Deutsche Bank-led group made a $640 million commercial construction loan for Trump International Hotel and Tower in Chicago in 2005. It was one project loan, distinct from later private-wealth loans for Doral and the Washington hotel. A 2008 payment dispute led to litigation; the parties settled in 2009. The report does not establish that the loan was an aggregate across Trump properties or involved foreign-intelligence leverage.
proposal.description_long: In 2005, Deutsche Bank and other lenders provided a $640 million construction loan for Trump International Hotel and Tower in Chicago. The Washington Post reported that this was one commercial real-estate loan and that the bank later syndicated much of it, reducing its own exposure. In 2008, Trump did not pay $334 million due on the loan and sued Deutsche Bank, arguing that the financial crisis was unforeseeable and seeking $3 billion in damages. The parties settled out of court in 2009, and the bank’s commercial mortgage unit did not do business with Trump again. The Post described the earlier relationship as including a separate $125 million 1998 loan for 40 Wall Street and another loan for Trump World Tower. Later loans for Doral and the Washington hotel came from Deutsche Bank’s private-banking division. The Chicago loan date is reported only by year. The proposed entry keeps that single commercial loan distinct from other properties and financing arrangements; it does not imply an aggregate $640 million loan package, foreign-intelligence leverage, or concealed subpoena information.

Those broader statements in the held synopsis are not substantiated by the cited source. The corrected date is June 9, 2025, and the source supports the membership change, not the effects of future committee advice.

The revised entry is limited to the dated appellate disposition and the scope of the court’s ruling. It preserves the divided procedural result rather than flattening it into a single finding.

proposal.title: Trump Calls MS-13 Members “Animals” at California Roundtable
proposal.description_short: At a May 16, 2018 White House roundtable, Trump said “These are animals” during a discussion of MS-13 gang members.
proposal.description_medium: At a May 16, 2018 White House roundtable about California sanctuary policies, President Donald Trump discussed MS-13 gang members and said, “These are animals.” The archived transcript places the phrase directly after his reference to MS-13. This supports a contextualized account of the remark, not the claim that he described immigrants generally as animals.
proposal.description_long: At a May 16, 2018 White House roundtable on California sanctuary policies, President Donald Trump discussed immigration enforcement and members of the MS-13 gang. The archived transcript places his phrase, “These are animals,” immediately after remarks about MS-13. The exchange followed Sheriff Margaret Mims’s account of a possible gang member whom local authorities could not report to ICE under a sanctuary-policy threshold. Trump then broadened his remarks about people entering the country before repeating, “These aren’t people. These are animals.” The transcript establishes the setting, wording and immediate context, but it does not support a title saying he called immigrants collectively “animals.” It also does not place the remark at a 2019 rally. This proposal ties the claim to the cited passage and avoids inferring a broader referent than the transcript demonstrates. The archived record is primary evidence of what was said at the roundtable; it does not resolve how every listener interpreted the wording.
